name: Baccharis

priority: mature mid-stem leaf blade width and outline (mm)
distribution and number of marginal leaf teeth

season and habitat only as supporting context
study_strategy.warning: A white fluffy fruiting shrub is not enough for species ID: both species are dioecious and produce white pappus on female plants. Leaf widths overlap at 3–5 mm; confirm with mature cypsela ribs where possible.
shared_traits: Woody or shrubby composites with alternate simple leaves
Numerous small capitula with involucral phyllaries
Male and female flowers usually on separate plants (dioecious)
Discoid heads have no showy ray florets; staminate and pistillate heads usually occur on different plants.
Fruiting pistillate heads develop cypselae carrying a conspicuous bristly pappus; count cypsela ribs only on mature fruits.

look_here_first: Find a woody shrub with alternate resin-dotted leaves and many tiny rayless, unisexual flower heads. For the two local learner species, compare mature leaf WIDTH and the tooth pattern first; confirm with mature female fruits: B. neglecta has 10-ribbed cypselae, B. salicifolia has 5-ribbed cypselae (Flora of North America).

handoffs.question: Verify reliable phyllary counts, leaf gland and margin thresholds for B. neglecta versus B. salicifolia before adding a hard dichotomous key.

handoffs.need: Acquire or reuse licensed paired leaf-with-scale, whole inflorescence and mature female cypsela rib macros (10 vs 5); no image substitutions or species install in genus builder.

quick_key.if: Mature mid-stem leaves mostly 1–2(–5) mm wide, linear to narrowly elliptic, usually entire or with only 2–3 shallow teeth; pyramidal branched head arrays
quick_key.then: Baccharis neglecta — confirm 10-ribbed mature cypselae (pappus 7–12 mm).

quick_key.if: Mature mid-stem leaves often broader, 3–20 mm wide, lanceolate-elliptic and frequently finely serrate along much of the margin; terminal compound corymb-like head arrays
quick_key.then: Baccharis salicifolia — confirm 5-ribbed mature cypselae (pappus 3–6 mm).

quick_key.if: Leaves fall in the 3–5 mm overlap or only male heads are available
quick_key.then: Provisional Baccharis sp.; photograph several matched leaves, full inflorescence, and revisit for mature female fruits before assigning species.

comparison_cards.caution: Do not confuse male/female head differences with species characters. White pappus is shared; fruit ribs are tiny and must be visible before claiming confirmation. Both may grow along streams.

overlap_and_cautions: Leaf width and serration vary by shoot age; compare leaves at matching positions.
Sex of heads differs between individuals; do not treat male-versus-female head differences as species differences.
Habitat alone is not a safe separator.
Leaf blade widths overlap around 3–5 mm; measure multiple mature mid-stem leaves, not one vigorous shoot or a reduced terminal bract.
B. salicifolia can have entire margins, so lack of serration does not automatically indicate B. neglecta.
Cypsela rib counts (10 vs 5) are the strongest documented fruit separator, but require fully mature female fruit and sharp macro images.
Pappus lengths apply to mature female fruit, not the shorter male-head pappus; compare equivalent stages.
FNA recognizes seasonal forms of B. salicifolia; avoid hard identification from season, habitat or general shrub outline alone.

local_source_pool_lookalikes.status: external look-alike, not installed in this pair
local_source_pool_lookalikes.separate: Broader, often three-nerved leaves with a few coarse teeth distally; cypselae 8–10-ribbed and longer pappus. Name is not a synonym of B. salicifolia.

local_source_pool_lookalikes.status: regional comparison, not installed in this pair
local_source_pool_lookalikes.separate: Main stem leaves commonly broader, rhombic/obovate, coarsely toothed toward tips; possible introgression with B. neglecta noted by FNA.
Inspect reproductive head, foliage texture and branching; don't assume every shrubby, fluffy-headed Asteraceae is Baccharis.
Willows bear catkins and different fruit; Baccharis has small composite heads with phyllaries and cypselae.

field_identification_sequence: Confirm Baccharis: woody, alternate leaves, tiny discoid heads, often male and female shrubs separate.
Measure several mature mid-stem leaves with a millimeter scale; compare leaf margin teeth.
Photograph entire inflorescence from enough distance to see panicle versus corymb branching.
If mature female fruit is present, count cypsela ribs (10 in B. neglecta, 5 in B. salicifolia); measure pappus as secondary confirmation.
If only male flowers or overlapping leaf dimensions are available, leave species tentative and revisit at fruiting.
